questions.question: Under a base-stock policy with integer level $S\geq0$, the inventory level is $I=S-X$, where $X\geq0$ is the integer lead-time demand. Which random variable is the backlog $I^-=\max\{-I,0\}$?
options: $(S-X)^+$, the amount by which $S$ exceeds the lead-time demand
$(X-S)^+$, the amount by which the lead-time demand exceeds $S$
$\min\{X,S\}$, the part of the lead-time demand met from stock
$X-S$, the signed difference of lead-time demand and base stock

questions.question: For a base-stock level $S\geq0$ and integer lead-time demand $X\geq0$, the expected backlog is $\mathbb{E}[I^-]=\sum_{j=S}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}(X>j)$. For $j\geq S$, what does the term $\mathbb{P}(X>j)$ measure?
options: The probability that the backlog equals exactly $j-S$ units
The probability that unit $j$ of the lead-time demand occurs and is short
The probability that unit $j+1$ of the lead-time demand occurs and is short
The probability that unit $j+1$ of the lead-time demand is met from stock

questions.question: Under a base-stock policy with level $S$, the inventory level is $I=S-X$, where the lead-time demand $X$ has mean $l\,\mathbb{E}[D]$. Which formula gives the expected on-hand stock $\mathbb{E}[I^+]$ from the expected backlog $\mathbb{E}[I^-]$?
options: $\mathbb{E}[I^+]=S-l\,\mathbb{E}[D]+\mathbb{E}[I^-]$
$\mathbb{E}[I^+]=S-l\,\mathbb{E}[D]-\mathbb{E}[I^-]$
$\mathbb{E}[I^+]=l\,\mathbb{E}[D]-S+\mathbb{E}[I^-]$
$\mathbb{E}[I^+]=(S-l\,\mathbb{E}[D])^+$

questions.question: For a base-stock policy with integer level $S\geq0$ and integer lead-time demand $X\geq0$, by how much does the expected backlog $\mathbb{E}[(X-S)^+]$ change when the level is raised from $S$ to $S+1$?
options: It falls by $\mathbb{P}(X\leq S)$
It falls by $\mathbb{P}(X=S)$
It falls by $\mathbb{P}(X\geq S)$
It falls by $\mathbb{P}(X>S)$

questions.question: For integer lead-time demand $X\geq0$ with mean $l\,\mathbb{E}[D]$, the expected backlog at base-stock level $S$ is $l\,\mathbb{E}[D]-\sum_{j=0}^{S-1}\mathbb{P}(X>j)$. What does this give for $\mathbb{E}[I^-]$ when $S=0$?
options: $l\,\mathbb{E}[D]-\mathbb{P}(X>0)$
$\mathbb{E}[D]$
$l\,\mathbb{E}[D]$
$\mathbb{P}(X>0)$

questions.question: Under a base-stock policy with level $S=1$, the lead-time demand $X$ has pmf $\mathbb{P}(X=0)=0.1$, $\mathbb{P}(X=1)=0.2$, $\mathbb{P}(X=2)=0.3$, $\mathbb{P}(X=3)=0.25$, $\mathbb{P}(X=4)=0.15$. What is the expected backlog $\mathbb{E}[(X-S)^+]$?

Only the mean $l\,\mathbb{E}[D]=3.2$ and the tail values $G_X(j)=\mathbb{P}(X>j)=0.95,\,0.80,\,0.60,\,0.35$ for $j=0,1,2,3$ of an integer lead-time demand $X$ are known. Using them, what is $\mathbb{E}[I^-]$ when the order-up-to level is $S=3$?

Under a base-stock policy, the expected on-hand stock at level $S=5$ is $\mathbb{E}[I^+]=1.6$, and the lead-time demand satisfies $\mathbb{P}(X\leq5)=0.85$. What is the expected on-hand stock $\mathbb{E}[I^+]$ at level $S=6$?
A base-stock policy uses level $S=-2$, so the inventory level is $I=-2-X$, where the integer lead-time demand $X\geq0$ has mean $l\,\mathbb{E}[D]=3$. What is the expected backlog $\mathbb{E}[I^-]$?

Under a base-stock policy, the lead-time demand $X$ takes values in $\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$ with $\mathbb{P}(X=5)>0$ and $\mathbb{E}[X]=2.4$. What is the smallest integer level $S$ with expected backlog $\mathbb{E}[(X-S)^+]=0$?

Under a base-stock policy with level $S$, the lead-time demand $X$ has mean $l\,\mathbb{E}[D]$. How does the mean plug-in $(l\,\mathbb{E}[D]-S)^+$ compare with the expected backlog $\mathbb{E}[(X-S)^+]$ for every $S$ and every distribution of $X$?
options: The plug-in is never smaller, so it is a safe upper bound on the backlog
The plug-in is never larger, so it can only understate the backlog
The two agree whenever $S\geq l\,\mathbb{E}[D]$, since both are then $0$
The two always agree, since expectation passes through the positive part

questions.question: For an integer base-stock level $S\geq1$ and integer lead-time demand $X\geq0$, the finite form of the expected backlog subtracts $\sum_{j=0}^{S-1}\mathbb{P}(X>j)$ from $\mathbb{E}[X]$. Which quantity does this sum equal?
options: $\mathbb{E}[\min\{X,S\}]$, the expected lead-time demand met from stock
$\mathbb{E}[(S-X)^+]$, the expected stock left on hand at the end
$\mathbb{P}(X\leq S)$, the probability that the stock covers the demand
$\mathbb{E}[(X-S)^+]$, the expected lead-time demand that is short

questions.question: A base-stock policy has holding cost $h>0$ and backlog cost $b>0$ per unit per period, and integer lead-time demand $X$. How does the smallest level $S^*$ minimising $c(S)=h\,\mathbb{E}[(S-X)^+]+b\,\mathbb{E}[(X-S)^+]$ respond when the ratio $b/h$ increases?
options: It strictly increases, because $b/(h+b)$ strictly increases with $b/h$
It decreases, because the rule uses $h/(h+b)$, which falls as $b/h$ rises
It does not change, because $S^*$ is set by the lead-time demand alone
It does not decrease, but it may stay put, because $F_X$ moves in steps

questions.question: A base-stock policy has holding cost $h=1$ and backlog cost $b=4$ per unit per period, and the lead-time demand satisfies $\mathbb{P}(X>6)=0.3$. For the average cost $c(S)=h\,\mathbb{E}[I^+]+b\,\mathbb{E}[I^-]$, what is $c(7)-c(6)$?

A base-stock policy has $h=1$, $b=7$, and lead-time demand $X$ with $\mathbb{E}[X]=2.48$ and $F_X(S)=0.10,0.30,0.55,0.80,0.87,0.93,0.97,1$ for $S=0,1,\ldots,7$. What is the smallest level $S^*$ minimising $c(S)=h\,\mathbb{E}[I^+]+b\,\mathbb{E}[I^-]$?

A base-stock policy uses $S=4$; the lead-time demand has mean $l\,\mathbb{E}[D]=3$ and the expected backlog is $\mathbb{E}[I^-]=0.25$. With $h=1$ and $b=6$ per unit per period, what is the average cost $c(4)=h\,\mathbb{E}[I^+]+b\,\mathbb{E}[I^-]$?

For a nonnegative random variable $X$ and an integer $S\geq0$, the identity $\mathbb{E}[(X-S)^+]=\sum_{j=S}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}(X>j)$, summed over integers $j$, is used to compute the expected base-stock backlog. Which property of $X$ is essential for this identity?
options: $X$ is bounded, so that only finitely many terms of the sum are nonzero
$X$ is a sum of independent period demands over the lead time
$X$ exceeds $S$ with positive probability, so that a backlog can occur
$X$ takes only integer values, so short units can be counted one by one

questions.question: A base-stock policy has holding cost $h=0$ and backlog cost $b>0$, and the integer lead-time demand $X\geq0$ has finite mean $\mathbb{E}[X]$ and satisfies $\mathbb{P}(X>j)>0$ for every integer $j$. Which statement about minimising $c(S)=h\,\mathbb{E}[I^+]+b\,\mathbb{E}[I^-]$ over integer $S$ is correct?
options: $c$ is still convex in $S$, so a minimiser exists and the critical fraction finds it
$S=0$ minimises $c$, because without holding cost no stock needs to be kept
$c$ strictly decreases in $S$, so no integer level minimises it
The minimiser is the smallest $S$ with $F_X(S)\geq1$, since $b/(h+b)=1$

questions.question: Period demands are iid and uniform on $\{0,1,2\}$, the lead time is $l=2$ periods, and the base-stock level is $S=2$. What is the expected backlog $\mathbb{E}[(X-S)^+]$, where $X=D_1+D_2$ is the lead-time demand?
A base-stock policy has $h=1$, $b=3$, and lead-time demand $X$ uniform on $\{0,1,2,3\}$. Which integer levels $S$ minimise $c(S)=h\,\mathbb{E}[(S-X)^+]+b\,\mathbb{E}[(X-S)^+]$?
options: $S=2$ and $S=3$, with equal cost
$S=2$ only, the unique minimiser
$S=3$ only, the unique minimiser
$S=1$ and $S=2$, with equal cost
